case_studies.title: Understanding Data Temporality Impact on Large Language Models Pre-training
case_studies.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are typically trained on shuffled corpora, yielding models whose knowledge is frozen at train time and whose temporal grounding remains poorly understood. In this work, we study the impact of pre-training dynamics on the acquisition of time-sensitive factual knowledge, focusing specifically on data ordering. Our main contributions are twofold. First, we introduce a comprehensive benchmark of over 7,000 temporally grounded questions and an evaluation protocol that enables analysis of whether models correctly associate facts with their corresponding time periods. case_studies.summary: This research investigates how the order of data affects the training of large language models, creating a benchmark to test their understanding of time-sensitive facts. The authors built a comprehensive test of over 7,000 questions to evaluate the models' temporal grounding. The result is a better understanding of how data temporality impacts large language models.
case_studies.it_breakdown: Not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work, as it focuses on the training of large language models rather than cloud infrastructure management. If your organisation uses large language models, this research may be of interest to data scientists or AI engineers. No immediate action is required for IT infrastructure managers.
case_studies.score_reasoning: Novelty is somewhat low because IT engineers may be familiar with the general concept of temporal groundings in LLMs, but the specific benchmark and evaluation protocol are new. Relevance is high because this directly affects how LLM APIs are used and understood. case_studies.title: Byte-Exact Deduplication in Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Three-Regime Empirical Analysis Across Public Benchmarks
case_studies.abstract: This preprint presents an empirical analysis of byte-exact chunk-level deduplication in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines. We measure context reduction across three distinct operating regimes: clean academic retrieval (0.16% byte reduction on 22.2M BeIR passages), constructed enterprise patterns (24.03% reduction), and multi-turn conversational AI (80.34% reduction). To validate quality preservation, we conducted a cross-vendor 5-judge calibrated panel evaluation across four production APIs (Google Gemini 2.5 Flash, Anthropic Claude Sonnet 4.6, Meta Llama 3.3 70B, and OpenAI GPT-5
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of efficient data storage by developing a method for byte-exact deduplication in Retrieval-Augmented Generation pipelines. The authors built and tested this method across three operating regimes, resulting in significant byte reduction. This method can help reduce storage needs in certain AI applications.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage cloud infrastructure for AI applications, consider implementing byte-exact deduplication to reduce storage costs: step 1, assess your current storage usage, step 2, evaluate the feasibility of deduplication in your Retrieval-Augmented Generation pipelines, step 3, test and deploy the deduplication method to optimize storage efficiency.

case_studies.title: When Retrieval Hurts Code Completion: A Diagnostic Study of Stale Repository Context
case_studies.abstract: Context: Retrieval-augmented code generation relies on cross-file repository context, but retrieved snippets may come from obsolete project states. Objectives: We study whether temporally stale repository snippets act as harmless noise or actively induce current-state-incompatible code. Methods: We conduct a controlled diagnostic study on a curated 17-sample set of production-helper signature changes from five Python repositories. case_studies.summary: This research studied how outdated code snippets in repositories can affect code completion, building a diagnostic study to compare the impact of current and stale repository context. The result showed that stale snippets can induce incompatible code, posing a potential problem for developers. The study aimed to understand whether these snippets are harmless or actively cause issues.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage code repositories, here is what to do: ensure that your code completion tools are configured to prioritize current repository context, review your repository's snippet retrieval settings to minimize the use of stale snippets, and consider implementing freshness checks for retrieved code snippets.
case_studies.score_reasoning: Research paper with limited IT relevance. While studying retrieval-augmented code generation is related to AI, the specifics of this paper do not directly affect how IT engineers work. Novelties in AI maturity, and potential monetization are present, but not applicable in the next 90 days.

case_studies.title: Reducing Political Manipulation with Consistency Training
case_studies.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) exhibit systematic political bias across a variety of sensitive contexts. We find that LLMs handle counterpart topics from opposing political sides asymmetrically. We refer to this phenomenon as covert political bias and identify 7 categories of techniques through which it operates. We propose two metrics for covert bias: Sentiment Consistency measures symmetry in rhetoric and framing across paired political prompts; Helpfulness Consistency measures symmetric depth and engagement. To reduce both types of covert bias, we introduce Political Consistency Training (PCT
case_studies.summary: This research addresses the problem of political bias in large language models by introducing a new training method called Political Consistency Training, which reduces covert bias by making the models more symmetric in their responses to opposing political views. The researchers built two metrics to measure this bias and applied the new training method to achieve more balanced results. This does not directly affect cloud infrastructure management.
case_studies.it_breakdown: Not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work, as it focuses on natural language processing and machine learning model training, but IT teams supporting AI applications may be interested in the broader implications of reducing bias in AI systems.
case_studies.score_reasoning: Novelty and relevance are somewhat related to IT, but the value score is low due to a lack of direct application to IT infrastructure. The paper is more focused on addressing a social issue.

case_studies.title: Declarative Data Services: Structured Agentic Discovery for Composing Data Systems
case_studies.abstract: Agentic discovery has shown that LLM-driven search can find novel algorithms, designs, and code under benchmark conditions. Translating the paradigm to multi-system data backends surfaces a harder problem: the search space is heterogeneous, the verifier is whether a deployed stack actually runs, and composition knowledge is unevenly captured in pretraining. Unbounded agentic discovery, a coding agent iterating on failure-log feedback, fails to converge consistently on a working stack even when iteration and explicit composition knowledge are added. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of composing data systems by introducing Declarative Data Services (DDS), a new approach that helps build and deploy working data stacks. The authors built DDS to address the challenges of heterogeneous search spaces and uneven composition knowledge in multi-system data backends. The result is a more efficient and consistent way to discover and deploy data systems.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage cloud data infrastructure, here is what to do: review your current data system composition methods, consider implementing Declarative Data Services (DDS) to improve efficiency and consistency, and assess the potential benefits of DDS for your organization's specific use case.
